analysis.summary: Kubernetes v1.35.0-rc.0 主要修复了admission控制中的竞争条件bug和alpha API警告问题，同时升级了Go版本以提升构建安全性。
key_changes: 修复alpha API版本差异警告问题 - [PR #135327](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135327)
Admission控制中命名空间查找回退机制优化 - [PR #135359](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135359)
important_bugfixes: 修复alpha API在apiserver启动时产生不必要的版本警告日志 - [PR #135327](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135327) - **影响：** 减少生产环境日志噪音，避免误导性警告信息
修复ValidatingAdmissionPolicy在新建命名空间后立即创建工作负载时出现虚假'namespace not found'错误 - [PR #135359](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135359) - **影响：** 防止admission控制误拒合法请求，提升工作负载创建可靠性
performance_improvements: 升级Go语言版本到1.25.4，包含运行时性能优化和安全补丁 - [PR #135492](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135492) - **提升：** 潜在的内存和CPU效率改进，具体数据需实测验证
recommendations: 建议在测试环境中充分验证ValidatingAdmissionPolicy的行为，特别是命名空间创建后的工作负载部署场景
升级前检查是否使用了alpha API，确保版本兼容性
由于是Release Candidate版本，不建议直接在生产环境部署，等待正式版发布
analysis.risk_assessment: 整体风险评估：中等风险。作为RC版本，可能存在未发现的边缘情况。建议的升级时机：在测试集群验证无误后，可考虑在非关键生产环境小范围试用。需要特别关注admission控制策略的稳定性和Go版本升级后的运行时表现。

135359.title: Fallback to live ns lookup on admission if lister cannot find namespace
135359.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Makes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy behave like other admission plugins (webhook admission, namespace lifecycle admission) which fall back to looking up live containing namespace objects if the lister is stale and does not contain a just-created namespace

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #135352

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

134023.title: Alpha API warnings printed to apiserver logs on startup
134023.body:
### What happened?

After upgrading from 1.34.0 to 1.34.1, warnings about alpha APIs are being printed to the kube-apiserver log on startup:

```

2025-09-11T18:33:21.482583037Z stderr F I0911 18:33:21.482494       1 server.go:152] "Golang settings" GOGC="" GOMAXPROCS="" GOTRACEBACK=""
2025-09-11T18:33:22.518763498Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518574       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1alpha1
2025-09-11T18:33:22.518788514Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518603       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=storage.k8s.io/v1alpha1

2025-09-11T18:33:22.518805327Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518652       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=internal.apiserver.k8s.io/v1alpha1
2025-09-11T18:33:22.518807747Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518657       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1
2025-09-11T18:33:22.518813631Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518663       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1
2025-09-11T18:33:22.518816398Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518668       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3
2025-09-11T18:33:22.518818657Z stderr F W0911 18:33:22.518673       1 api_enablement.go:112] alpha api enabled with emulated version 1.34 instead of the binary's version 1.34.1, this is unsupported, proceed at your own risk: api=node.k8s.io/v1alpha1
```

### What did you expect to happen?

No spurious logs

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run Kubernetes 1.34.1, look at apiserver logs

### Anything else we need to know?

Appears to be related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133058, which should be checking major+minor versions only, not patch version - as the emulated version will never have a patch version set.

135352.title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy namespace lookup raced newly created namespaces, produces spurious "namespace not found" rejections
135352.body:
### What happened?

When creating new workload (observed with Deployment and StatefulSet) immediately after creating its namespace, there is a possibility that watch case has not yet caught up to the new namespace existing.

Naively, this would result in frequent failures, but apiserver guards against this by falling back to live client when namespace was `NotFound`. Example: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ab3e83f73424a18f298a0050440af92d2d7c4720/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/predicates/namespace/matcher.go#L88

The issue happens infrequently but can be forced by overriding informer lister to always return NotFound for a specific namespace (see repro instructions below). This way, the call to informer's lister would always fail, while the call to client would remain unaffected - this would force the fallback path, ensuring it is present.

### What did you expect to happen?

No 404 errors when creating StatefulSets in existing namespaces - even immediately after ns creation.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?



```
--- a/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/listers/core/v1/namespace.go
+++ b/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/listers/core/v1/namespace.go
@@ -20,7 +20,6 @@ package v1

 import (
        corev1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
-       errors "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors"
        labels "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/labels"
        listers "k8s.io/client-go/listers"
        cache "k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache"
@@ -47,17 +46,3 @@ type namespaceLister struct {
 func NewNamespaceLister(indexer cache.Indexer) NamespaceLister {
        return &namespaceLister{listers.New[*corev1.Namespace](indexer, corev1.Resource("namespace"))}
 }
-
-// Get retrieves the Namespace from the index for a given name.
-// Objects returned here must be treated as read-only.
-// This method overrides the embedded Get to add custom logic.
-func (nl *namespaceLister) Get(name string) (*corev1.Namespace, error) {
-       // 1. Check if the requested namespace is "lalala"
-       if name == "lalala" {
-               // 2. Return not found error if it is
-               return nil, errors.NewNotFound(corev1.Resource("namespace"), name)
-       }
-       // 3. Otherwise, use the parent implementation from the embedded ResourceIndexer
-       return nl.ResourceIndexer.Get(name)
-}
-
```


Steps to reproduce:

  1. Apply the diff above to apiserver code.
  2. Set up a cluster using that apiserver.
  3. Create the namespace "lalala"
  4. Create a StatefulSet in that namespace
  5. Observe the request failing with 404 - it should succeed despite the damaged lister code

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

Based on our (limited) set of observations, we believe the regression happened between 1.32 and 1.33

### Cloud provider

Observations were made in GKE

### OS version

N/A

### Install tools

_No response_

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_
